question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Awkward in movement or manner
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Awkward"** means lacking skill or dexterity; lacking grace or ease in movement. (अजीब)

 
 
• **Example: **His awkward movements made it clear he was nervous.
 
 
 
• **"Clumsy" **refers to being awkward in movement or manner. It describes someone who often has accidents because they do not behave in a careful, controlled way. (अनाड़ी)
 
 
• **Example: **She made a clumsy attempt to catch the ball and missed.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the word 'clumsy' is a suitable one-word substitute for 'awkward in movement or manner'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Alert **(सतर्क): Quick to notice any unusual and potentially dangerous or difficult circumstances; vigilant.

 
 
• **Example:** The guard was alert to any sign of trouble.
 
 
 
• **Imbalanced **(असंतुलित): Lacking balance; uneven in distribution or allocation.
 
 
• **Example: **His imbalanced diet led to various health issues.
 
 
 
• **Clownish** (मसखरा): Behaving in a silly or funny way.
 
 
• **Example:** His clownish antics always made the children laugh.
